reject_reason: other: invalid comparison - the library computes single-precision float GEMM (float* matrices, __m256, _mm256_fmadd_ps; no double code anywhere in MatrixMul.cpp) while the baseline Benchmarks/EigenBenchmark.cpp multiplies MatrixXd (double) through MKL dgemm (the README itself names MKL's avx2_dgemm_kernel_0), so the 'identically or slightly faster than Eigen (MKL+TBB)' claim compares SGEMM against DGEMM
tier_reason: Benchmark code (Benchmarks/EigenBenchmark.cpp, MatrixMult/MatrixMul.cpp main), MSVC 2017 flags and the i7-8700K are public, but the comparison is not like-for-like (float vs double, which gives float twice the AVX2 FMA width and half the memory traffic), and the numbers are a first-party graph (Benchmark1.png) of single timed runs, so it cannot be A; at most C if kept.

corrections.workload: Multithreaded SINGLE-precision (float) square matrix multiplication C = A*B in the library, one timed call per run, N from 10 to 15,000; the Eigen baseline multiplies double-precision MatrixXd with the MKL backend (dgemm), so precisions differ.
corrections.claimed_speedup: README: 'Current implementation runs identically or slightly faster than Eigen (MKL+TBB) for all test cases (tested up to N=15K)'. Benchmark1.png plots N^3/runtime (x10^9): the library ('MM') peaks near 157 at N=6000 vs Eigen(MKL+TBB) near 132, and the two lines are about even at N=13000-15000 (about 130-142); MM is behind Eigen at N=400, N=600-700 and N=13000 (read from the graph). These are float GEMM results against a double-precision MKL dgemm baseline, so they do not show a like-for-like win.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: MSVC 2017, x64 Release plus /O2 /Ot /Gy /arch:AVX2 /fp:fast /std:c++17; hand-written AVX/FMA float intrinsics (_mm256_fmadd_ps), software prefetching, runtime-detected block sizes. The Eigen benchmark (Benchmarks/EigenBenchmark.cpp) defines EIGEN_USE_MKL_ALL, uses MatrixXd (double) and sets 12 MKL/Eigen threads; Eigen/MKL/TBB versions not stated.
corrections.caveats: Precision mismatch: MatrixMul.cpp stores matrices as float and uses __m256/_mm256_fmadd_ps throughout (no double path), while EigenBenchmark.cpp uses MatrixXd and the README says MKL's avx2_dgemm_kernel_0 ran, so the library's float GEMM is compared with MKL's double GEMM. On AVX2, float FMA throughput is twice that of double, so 'about equal to MKL dgemm' implies well below MKL sgemm; no float-vs-float comparison exists. The graph's peak (N^3/runtime about 157e9, i.e. about 314 GFLOPS float) is also far below the i7-8700K's float FMA peak (derived estimate). Each point is a single timed call with 12 threads on one desktop CPU; numbers exist only in Benchmark1.png and benchmark.xlsx. NumpyBenchmark.py times np.dot at n=1000 only. Windows-only (Win32 affinity API, MSVC intrinsics/_aligned_malloc). No license file (raw LICENSE, LICENSE.md, LICENSE.txt all 404; repo page shows none), so reference-only. README says the build without software prefetching is about 15% faster on this CPU. Single author, last commit 2018-11-28.

notes: Correctness-of-comparison bug: float SGEMM timed against Eigen MatrixXd on MKL dgemm, so the 'faster than MKL' claim is invalid (like the SIMD-MT/stb-zip precedents of computing something different). If kept under keep-and-document, tier C with that shortcoming; metadata (18 stars, 2 forks, no license, last commit 2018-11-28, not fork/archived) checked and correct.
